description: Expecting modest growth in M2 and M3 monetary aggregates over coming months consistent with the contemplated reserve conditions
justification: Expecting "modest" monetary aggregate growth signals constrained monetary expansion consistent with the tightening policy stance.

description: Adopting symmetric intermeeting guidance allowing for slightly greater or slightly lesser reserve restraint as acceptable during the intermeeting period
justification: Symmetric guidance allows flexibility for adjustments in either direction, representing a neutral stance for intermeeting policy implementation.

description: Increasing the discount rate by 50 basis points
justification: The 50 basis point discount rate increase reinforces the restrictive monetary policy stance alongside the federal funds rate increase.

description: Increasing the federal funds rate by 50 basis points and increasing the degree of pressure on reserve positions
justification: A 50 basis point federal funds rate increase represents significant monetary tightening designed to combat emerging inflationary pressures.

description: Setting monitoring range for growth of domestic nonfinancial debt at 3-7% for 1995, down from the previous 4-8% range
justification: Lowering the debt monitoring range indicates slightly more restrictive expectations for debt growth in the economy.

description: Release of policy statement indicating that the Federal Reserve will continue to monitor developments but that current actions are expected to be sufficient at least for a time to meet the objective of sustained noninflationary growth
justification: The statement's indication that current actions should be sufficient "at least for a time" provides slightly accommodative forward guidance by suggesting a pause in the tightening cycle.

description: Setting tentative ranges for 1995 monetary growth of 1-5% for M2 and 0-4% for M3, measured from fourth quarter 1994 to fourth quarter 1995
justification: Maintains existing monetary growth ranges without change, representing continuity in the monetary framework rather than accommodation or restriction.
